what_it_is: A statistical re-evaluation of GSM-Symbolic's headline finding that LLMs lose accuracy on template-generated variants of GSM8K questions (p.1). Re-evaluating 20 open-weight models with bootstrapped generalised linear mixed models that treat questions as random effects (the language-as-fixed-effect fallacy, p.2), it finds that only 8 show significant changes under the original prompt format (p.1). It also shows that the variants' integers are shifted towards larger values than GSM8K's (K-S 0.12, p < 0.001), and controlling for this large-number effect accounts for significance in half of the remaining cases (p.1). Holm-Bonferroni correction is applied across models (p.5). Alternative prompt formats then separate failure profiles: variable binding, arithmetic and dual-task interference (p.1).
size: 20 open-weight models; GSM-Symbolic's 100 questions with 50 variants each (p.1)
evaluation: final-answer accuracy, analysed with GLMMs with per-question random effects, bootstrapped, Holm-corrected across models (p.1, p.5)

overlap_with_engtrace: Its critique has three parts, and EngTrace's analyses already meet each. (1) Items as random effects: the paper treats questions as random effects (p.2). EngTrace's full-run analyses resample templates for every interval and test model differences by sign-flip permutation over per-template differences, because 'instances of a template are not' independent; item-level McNemar is reported beside them only for contrast (full_run_28092026/results/RESULTS.md, lines 3 and 23; D-111). (2) Multiplicity: EngTrace applies Holm across the 55 pairs and across the eleven models in the cliff and paraphrase analyses (RESULTS.md lines 23 and 85; state brief section 4). (3) A confound between original and variant: the paraphrase arm keeps the original's numbers as a multiset (state brief section 4), so a magnitude shift like GSM-Symbolic's cannot arise there. What remains open is the complexity analysis: the cliff compares different templates in different tiers, so tier is confounded with whatever else differs between those templates; RESULTS.md checks two such factors (rows left unusable at the output cap, and the nine symbolic templates, line 101), and the paper should not read the gap as an effect of difficulty alone. Its message also matches EngTrace's own paraphrase result: no model's paraphrase difference survives Holm.
notes: (1) The venue rests on the arXiv comment alone. (2) It re-uses GSM-Symbolic's main set only; the harder variants and added clauses are out of its scope (p.1, footnote 1).
